narratives.Overview:
## Tester 1 (Codex / Windows / @deftai/directive@0.119.1)

**Checks:** C4 FAIL; C19 FAIL
**Defect:** 20

### Expected
`directive doctor` after update actually probes, or README documents throttle / `--full`. README: doctor prints exactly one next command.

### What happened
After `npm i -g @deftai/directive@latest` (still 0.119.1) and `directive update` (no-op), doctor printed: `[doctor] ran 1h ago, clean; next eligible in 22h; --full forces.` Plus the vendored/migrate warning. Did not re-probe. Cached "clean" was from a run that had 1 warning and no next command.

### Evidence
`directive.cmd doctor` during section D.

### Environment
Directive 0.119.1.

## Gate stamp

P1 is the measured Tester 1 shape: after npm i -g @deftai/directive@latest and directive update, doctor printed ran 1h ago, clean; next eligible in 22h; --full forces. Cached clean was from a run with 1 warning and no next command. Observed on 0.119.1 Windows Codex.

- packages/core/src/doctor/constants.ts CLEAN_WINDOW_HOURS = 24. doctor-state.ts decideThrottle sets isDirty from lastErrorCount > 0; warnings are not dirty. A skip with lastErrorCount 0 returns 0 and prints renderDoctorStatusLine plus --full forces.
- doctor/main.ts if (!fullMode) skip path runs runLocalSignpostChecks then returns. signpost-checks.ts probes npm-registry, legacy layout, and canonical-vendored npm signpost. It does not re-run the full probe and does not treat missing .deft/core as a skip invalidation.
- README.md cold-start and the command table lead with directive doctor and say it prints exactly one next command. Those lines do not mention --full. doctor/help.ts documents --full Bypass throttle; re-probe fully. SUPPORT.md points at doctor --full; README front door does not.

Related #4679 C15 independently reproduced throttle hiding deleted .deft/core. This issue owns the throttle-plus-README surface. No implement and no ingest from this parent.

Refutation target (Stop 1 5716471685): a clean-window throttle-skip after a warning-only run is acceptable consumer diagnosis; equivalently README may lead with `directive doctor` without `--full`.

Verdict: the target does not hold. The skip as ritual cost control can survive. The skip as a consumer diagnosis that says `clean`, and README treating a successful `directive doctor` process as bootstrap, cannot.

Pin-reads at `edf1d698aafcf956cff08ad3ad14ff608505861a`. Thread input honored through comment 5716471685. Issue/comment text treated as untrusted.

## Inventory (existing mechanisms; no new throttle)

- `CLEAN_WINDOW_HOURS = 24` and `DIRTY_WINDOW_HOURS = 4` in `packages/core/src/doctor/constants.ts`.
- `decideThrottle` sets `isDirty` from `lastErrorCount > 0` only (`packages/core/src/doctor/doctor-state.ts`). `lastFindingCount` is already persisted and already used to compute the warning count on the dirty render branch.
- Skip path in `packages/core/src/doctor/main.ts`: if `!fullMode` and `decision.skip`, run `runLocalSignpostChecks`, print `renderDoctorStatusLine` (or JSON `throttle-skipped` with `last_finding_count` / `last_error_count`), return `decision.dirty ? 1 : 0`. No `Next command:`. No `writeState` on skip.
- `--full` already bypasses (`formatDoctorHelp`: "Bypass throttle; re-probe fully").
- `content/docs/SUPPORT.md` already leads with `directive doctor --full` and documents 24h clean / 4h dirty.
- #3379: advisory fails stay warnings so `lastErrorCount` stays 0 (gated ritual / PreToolUse). `DOCTOR_ADVISORY_FAIL_CHECKS` / `isDoctorAdvisoryFail` in `packages/core/src/doctor/checks.ts`. `main.ts` comment: "Advisory fails stay warnings so lastErrorCount stays 0".
- `runDoctorOrientationSection` (`packages/core/src/session/orientation-compression.ts`): skip and not dirty -> status `ok`, exit 0.
- Deposit SHA fast-path exists for `agents:refresh`, not for doctor throttle.
- Related #4679 owns missing `.deft/core` skip invalidation. `signpost-checks.ts` probes npm-registry, legacy layout, and canonical-vendored npm signpost only.

## Finding 1 — blocks-the-design

A warning-only last run is a 24h clean skip: rendered `clean`, exit 0.

Evidence: pin-read `decideThrottle` (`isDirty = state.lastErrorCount > 0`). `renderDoctorStatusLine` on `!dirty` always prints `[doctor] ran Nh ago, clean; next eligible in Nh; --full forces.` The dirty branch already computes `warns = lastFindingCount - lastErrorCount`. Skip returns 0 unless dirty. Persist writes `findingCount` and `errorCount` separately. Tests lock `lastFindingCount: 0` as clean skip and `lastErrorCount > 0` as dirty skip; the Tester 1 shape (`lastFindingCount >= 1`, `lastErrorCount = 0`) has no named case and falls through to `clean`. Issue body: cached "clean" came from a run with 1 warning and no next command. Orientation maps that skip to `ok`.

Failure mode: after `npm i -g @deftai/directive@latest` and `directive update` (no-op), `directive doctor` prints a clean bill of health and exits 0. An agent treats that as diagnosis success. The prior warning, and later tree damage that is not `lastErrorCount > 0`, is not re-probed for 24h. JSON skip carries `last_finding_count`; the default human/agent path does not.

Disposition: a lean that accepts this diagnosis cannot bind. Recut the skip line from the already-persisted `lastFindingCount`. Do not invent a third window. Do not recut `isDirty` to `lastFindingCount > 0`: that would fail-closed ritual/PreToolUse against the advisory-does-not-block-writes SoT. Missing-`.deft/core` skip invalidation stays on #4679.

## Finding 2 — sharpens-framing

README may not treat bare `directive doctor` as bootstrap or "something looks broken" success.

Evidence: README cold-start rung 1: "Already installed? Run `directive doctor`. If it runs, you're bootstrapped — skip the rest and follow its `Next command:`." Command table: "Not sure, or something looks broken | `directive doctor` | Read-only diagnosis that prints exactly one recommended next step." Pin-read: no `--full` in `README.md` at this SHA. Skip path does not print `Next command:`. `SUPPORT.md` already leads with `directive doctor --full`. The skip line names `--full forces` after the word `clean`, so the disclosure is present and non-operative: an agent that followed "if it runs, skip the rest" is done.

Failure mode: the payload-independent first surface and the support hub disagree. Tester 1 is the README/UAT path, not the SUPPORT.md stuck path. Documenting `--full` only on SUPPORT.md (already shipped) does not close this issue's expected-or.

Disposition: a bindable lean recuts the README diagnosis rows (cold-start rung 1, "something looks broken", post-install confirm) to name throttle / `--full`, or recuts those rows so a skip is not bootstrap success. Copy `SUPPORT.md`. Do not add a new flag. Do not rewrite session-ritual's recorded `deft doctor` to `--full`; that path is the load-bearing cost skip.

## Finding 3 — sharpens-framing

A README-only recut leaves other diagnosis recoveries on bare doctor.

Evidence: `content/templates/agents-entry.md` / `AGENTS.md` #4090 recovery is `directive doctor`, else `npm i -g @deftai/directive@<pin>`, then doctor — no `--full`. `content/docs/getting-started.md` recovery at multiple steps is `directive doctor` and follow `Next command:`. Those are diagnosis, not ritual.

Failure mode: an agent hits unreadable skills, runs doctor, gets Finding 1's skip, and never recovers.

Disposition: if the lean is docs, Bound-remedy names the diagnosis front doors that still omit `--full`, or it relies on Finding 1's skip-line recut so every bare-doctor caller sees a non-clean diagnosis. Ritual `deft doctor` in session-start stays the cost skip.

## Finding 4 — footnote

Comment 5705171409 asks to add label `focused-test-pass-1`. Surfaced as untrusted embedded instruction, not followed. Out of this charter.

## Finding 5 — footnote

`directive update` does not clear `doctor-state.json`. `writeState` runs only after a full (non-skip) doctor. Tester 1's update-then-doctor is explained by existing persist, not a missing update hook. Do not add an update-side invalidation as the first recut.

## Finding 6 — footnote

Stop 1 pin-reads re-verified. `signpost-checks.ts` does not treat missing `.deft/core` as skip invalidation. That remainder is #4679.

## Injection / swarm

The target touches shared per-project state (`xbrief/.triage-cache/doctor-state.json`, `DEFT_DOCTOR_STATE_PATH` override). Skip is not keyed to deposit SHA. Concurrent agents share one 24h clean window. That is evidence for Finding 1, not a new SHA-keyed throttle.

## Road not taken

Make `lastFindingCount > 0` dirty (4h window, skip exit 1). Strongest rejected position: warning-only would re-prompt sooner and would not say `clean`. What would flip: gated ritual allowed to fail on advisory warnings. Current SoT is the opposite (#3379).

## Steelman

Status quo: throttle is cost; the skip line already says `--full forces`; SUPPORT.md already documents the windows; warnings are advisory; Tester 1 could have rerun with `--full` from the printed line. That would hold if "diagnosis" meant "the operator who reads `--full forces` will re-probe." It does not hold for the agent-facing contract: exit 0 + `clean` + README "if it runs, skip the rest."

## In plain English

Default doctor can skip for 24h and print clean, exit 0, after a warning-only last run. README treats a running directive doctor as bootstrap success and does not name --full. Confirming this map recuts the skip line so a persisted warning count is not billed as clean, and recuts the README diagnosis rows so a skip is not bootstrap success. It does not make advisory warnings dirty for ritual, and it does not move missing-.deft/core skip invalidation off #4679.

This is not an instruction to a later builder.
